cases.description: When the JSON instance conforms to the schema, the validator should produce no ValidationMessage objects. The custom OutputFormat collects the messages into a List, which is expected to be empty.

cases.expected: A List containing at least two ValidationMessage objects (type mismatch for 'age' and null value for required 'name')
cases.description: The JSON instance violates the schema (wrong type for 'age' and missing required 'name'). The validator must return the collected validation messages via the OutputFormat.
Passing a null JsonNode should cause the method to throw a NullPointerException before any validation is performed.
If the OutputFormat argument is null the method must fail fast with a NullPointerException.
When the provided Consumer throws an unchecked exception, the validate method must not swallow it; the exception should propagate to the caller.

input.value: Consumer that sets a flag on the ExecutionContext

cases.expected: Flag on ExecutionContext is true after validation
cases.description: The Consumer supplied to the method should be executed exactly once. The test uses a mutable flag (e.g., AtomicBoolean) that the Consumer sets; after validation the flag must be true, confirming the Consumer was called.

cases.expected: A List containing at least one ValidationMessage indicating that the instance is not an object (type mismatch)
cases.description: The schema expects an object with properties; providing a JSON array should trigger a type‑mismatch validation message. The custom OutputFormat should collect that message.

cases.expected: A List containing two ValidationMessage objects (missing required 'age' and missing required 'name')
cases.description: When the instance is an empty object, the validator must report each required property that is absent.

group: Additional properties not allowed – unexpected field detection

cases.expected: A List containing one ValidationMessage indicating that property 'extra' is not allowed
cases.description: Assuming the schema has "additionalProperties": false, an unexpected property should be reported as a validation error.
If the Consumer argument is null the method should throw a NullPointerException before performing any validation.
A custom OutputFormat that counts validation messages should receive an empty list for a valid instance and therefore return 0.
When the instance violates the schema, the CountingOutputFormat should return the number of validation messages (at least two in this case).

group: OutputFormat throws unchecked exception – propagation test

cases.description: If the OutputFormat implementation throws an unchecked exception while processing the validation messages, the validate method must not catch it; the exception should propagate unchanged.

cases.expected: A List containing exactly one ValidationMessage (validation stops after first error)
cases.description: When the Consumer configures the ExecutionContext to fail fast, the validator should stop after the first detected error, resulting in a single ValidationMessage.

The JsonSchema instance is constructed from a schema JSON that contains a $ref pointing to a non‑existent definition. When validate(JsonNode, OutputFormat<T>, Consumer<ExecutionContext>) is invoked, the resolver should detect the missing reference and throw an IllegalArgumentException. The test verifies that the exception is propagated to the caller.
